text:
riley: Quick sync 50m ago we discussed splitting session-mesh. proposing a slightly different carve: prefix-cache, routing-core, affinity-proxy, health-sidecar. keeping affinity separate lets us iterate on session-homing heuristics without touching routing.

tara: Why four? feels like overfragmenting.

riley: Goal is isolation by concern: cache (hot KV), routing (decisioning), affinity (sticky heuristics + telemetry), health (safety checks + circuit-breakers). Each has different scaling and SLOs.

aj: I like separation for scaling. main risk is hop-latency and transactional semantics for writes that touch cache+routing. How do we keep writes atomic?
iley: Plan A: make writes idempotent and accept eventual consistency for certain writes (we already do this for prefix updates). Plan B: for ops that must be linearizable, route them through a coordinator (short-lived transaction service) that can be deprecated after migration.

sohail: Can we quantify the extra latency? if coordinator is used, what's the p50/p95 impact?
aj: Coordinator adds ~1.5ms median and ~5ms p95 in our perf bench when co-located. Without coordinator (eventual), median is ~0.3ms but p99 tail improves if we avoid cross-service sync.

tara: Migration story? we have millions of prefixes in the DB. moving to prefix-cache without downtime needs thought.

riley: Migration steps (sketch):
1) Deploy prefix-cache in read-only mode, shadow reads from monolith, fill cache lazily
2) Enable bulk warmup job for top-N hot prefixes (batched warmup with backpressure)
3) Open write-path behind feature flag to coordinator for linearizable ops; other writes go to monolith
4) Gradually flip routing-core to read from cache for reads, while writes still shadow to cache
5) Once cache has >95% hit for hot traffic and metrics stable, remove coordinator paths iteratively

tara: Bulk warmup sounds heavy. need throttles and progress metrics.

riley: Agreed. Warmup will be batched by tenant and bounded by RPS gate. We'll expose a warmup progress counter and ETA.

sohail: Observability checklist: per-service latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), cross-service distributed traces with request id, cache hit ratio, warmup progress, coordinator queue depth, and an end-to-end correctness test (synthetic workflow) failure rate.

aj: Add a regression detector too: if end-to-end p99 increases >12% or error budget burn spikes by 3x in 10m, auto-rollback.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: prefix-cache-v0.1 scheduled to canary pool (10% traffic).

riley: Rollout gates: start at 5% canary, wait 15m, then 10% for 1h with synthetic traffic ramp. If stable, 25% for 2h, then 50% overnight. Manual approval required for 100%.

tara: Who owns the compatibility contract (proto + headers + errors)? we need a documented surface and strict compatibility tests.
iley: Ownership: infra-storage owns prefix-cache API and compatibility tests. routing-core owns routing contract. we'll create a joint repo with compatibility harness (contract-test jobs).

sohail: Failure modes to document: cache divergence (stale prefixes), coordinator outage (write failures), affinity oscillation (sticky churn), and health-sidecar misreports. For each include recovery steps and mitigation.

aj: Add a debug mode to force RPC-only (no shared-mem fastpath) and a knob to simulate cold-cache for canaries. Operators need an easy toggle.

riley: Good call. Also include a plan to pin canary tenants to Dedicated hosts to reduce cross-AZ noise during testing.

infra-bot: ci-status: prefix-cache integration-tests passed (18/18). e2e smoke queued.

deploy-bot: smoke-run: e2e smoke passed against canary (basic read/write).

riley: Next docs: RFC follow-up with interface sketches, migration playbook, and runbook snippets for each failure mode. I'll open PRs and tag infra-storage + routing-core leads.

tara: Please include churn estimator (team effort + days) so PM can plan the sprint.

riley: Will add an initial estimate: 3 sprints for core extraction + 1 sprint for migration and polish (assuming green tests).

sohail: One more ops ask: make the coordinator a short-lived stateful job (not monolithic) so we can scale it independently and treat it as a canary path first.

aj: Agree. Also set a tight TTL on coordinator state to avoid long-lived locks.

riley: tagging @aj @tara @sohail @infra-bot for follow-up. Will send links to the perf runs and preliminary proto sketch in the PR.

tara: Thanks. I'll review the PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sohail: Same.

riley: End of thread.
